1. (Currently amended) A method for vehicle-to-vehicle communication, comprising: transmitting a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first transmission speed from a first vehicle; receiving a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a second vehicle via an infrared video sensor; analyzing the second sequence to determine vehicle proximity and safety conditions; and transmitting a safety message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second transmission speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the second speed is dynamically determined based on proximity and safety parameters of the second vehicle.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the second speed is set to accommodate the reception capability of the second vehicle.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity based on signal loss or degradation and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed and returns to a default transmission rate.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fourth speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth speed is different from the second speed and is independently determined based on the third vehicle's proximity and safety parameters.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed and is transmitted to improve vehicle-to-vehicle collision avoidance.

7. (Original) The method of claim 6, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

8. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received via an IR video sensor.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from two or more vehicles in proximity to the first vehicle.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of light pulses having a fifth speed based on the sequences of light pulses received from the two or more vehicles, wherein the fifth speed is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses to ensure all nearby vehicles can receive the safety message.

11. (Currently amended) An apparatus for vehicle-to-vehicle infrared communication, comprising: a processor; a memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first transmission speed; receive a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a vehicle via an infrared video sensor; analyze the second sequence to determine vehicle proximity and safety conditions; and transmit a safety message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second transmission speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the second speed is dynamically determined based on proximity and safety parameters of the vehicle.

12. 13. 17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the message is also transmitted via a wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network.

19. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the sequences of light pulses are received from one or more vehicles in proximity to the apparatus.
